title: Removing transfer marks
subtitle: How to remove water-soluble pen marks, heat-erasable marks, and chalk residue from finished embroidery.
excerpt: Transfer marks that remain after stitching must come out before the finished piece is pressed or framed. Each type of marker has a different removal method. The wrong removal step sets the marks permanently. This technique entry covers each type in order.
sourceNotes: Finishing technique synthesised from contemporary needlework practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Marks left on the fabric after the stitching is complete from whatever transfer method was used: water-soluble pen marks, heat-erasable pen marks, pounce chalk dots, or carbon paper traces.

content.text: is easiest to remove before pressing. Heat sets most marks. The single most common mistake in embroidery finishing is ironing before washing, which turns removable marks into permanent stains.
Soak the embroidery in cold clean water for ten minutes.
Lift and check that the marks have gone. If any remain, soak for a further ten minutes.
Do not iron until all marks are gone. Iron after, not before.
Press the embroidery with a warm to medium iron on the reverse side. The marks will disappear within seconds.
Steam press a second time to ensure the marks won't return if the piece is stored cold.
Shake the embroidery gently over a waste bin to dislodge loose chalk.
Brush lightly with a clean soft brush.
Wash the piece in cold water with gentle detergent to remove the last traces.

Carbon paper transfer marks are designed to wash out with the finished piece. Wash in cool water with a small amount of gentle detergent. Most marks disappear fully. If any trace remains, spot-treat with a clean damp cloth. Carbon paper residue that is covered by stitching does not need to be removed.
